Interpolate point measurements onto a grid

geo_interpolate.Rd

Predicts a numeric column of a point table at new locations by inverse-distance weighting (IDW) or ordinary kriging, both computed in C++. Distances are great-circle metres on longitude/latitude data and map units otherwise.

For kriging, give the variogram (model, nugget, psill, range) or leave psill and range as NULL to fit it from the data with gstat (gstat::fit.variogram()). The predictions and kriging variances match gstat::krige() for the same variogram. The fitted or given variogram is stored in attribute "variogram".

Both methods run in C++ on several cores; set the number with options(tidymapr.threads = n).

Usage

geo_interpolate(
  data,
  value,
  grid,
  method = c("idw", "kriging"),
  power = 2,
  maxdist = Inf,
  model = c("Exp", "Sph", "Gau"),
  nugget = 0,
  psill = NULL,
  range = NULL,
  variance = TRUE,
  name = "prediction"
)

Arguments

data

An sf point table.

value

<data-masking> Numeric column to interpolate.

grid

Where to predict: a terra::SpatRaster template (every cell centre is predicted) or an sf point table.

method

"idw" or "kriging".

power

IDW distance power (default 2).

maxdist

IDW search radius; samples farther away are ignored (default Inf, all samples).

model

Kriging variogram model: "Exp" (exponential), "Sph" (spherical) or "Gau" (Gaussian), with gstat's parameterisation.

nugget, psill, range

Variogram nugget, partial sill and range. psill and range default to a fit with gstat. range is in metres on longitude/latitude data and in map units otherwise.

variance

For kriging, also return the kriging variance? Skipping it (FALSE) makes large grids much faster.

name

Name of the prediction layer or column.

Value

For a raster grid, a SpatRaster with layer name (and "variance" for kriging). For an sf grid, the same table with these columns added.

References

Isaaks, E. H. and Srivastava, R. M. (1989). An Introduction to Applied Geostatistics. Oxford University Press.

Examples

sites <- geo_as_sf(geo_example_sites("wilhelm"), lon, lat)
bb <- sf::st_bbox(sites)
grid <- terra::rast(nrows = 20, ncols = 20, xmin = bb[["xmin"]],
  xmax = bb[["xmax"]], ymin = bb[["ymin"]], ymax = bb[["ymax"]],
  crs = "EPSG:4326")
idw <- geo_interpolate(sites, elevation, grid, power = 2)
idw
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 20, 20, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 0.013753, 0.0045315  (x, y)
#> extent      : 145.058, 145.333, -5.81424, -5.72361  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> name        :  prediction
#> min value   :   237.59271
#> max value   : 3631.580387

# Kriging with a given variogram (fit one with gstat by leaving
# psill and range NULL)
geo_interpolate(sites, elevation, grid, method = "kriging",
  model = "Exp", psill = 4e5, range = 8000)
#> class       : SpatRaster
#> size        : 20, 20, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#> resolution  : 0.013753, 0.0045315  (x, y)
#> extent      : 145.058, 145.333, -5.81424, -5.72361  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326)
#> source(s)   : memory
#> names       :  prediction,      variance
#> min values  :  356.799255,  32323.955311
#> max values  : 3543.455139, 376588.725393
